steps.tx: **Microscopic polyangiitis** or MPA is a systemic necrotizing small vessel vasculitis that characteristically lacks granulomatous inflammation. Clinically, it frequently presents as a severe pulmonary-renal syndrome featuring **rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis** and pulmonary capillaritis causing life-threatening **diffuse alveolar hemorrhage** requiring immediate intensive care.
steps.say: Microscopic polyangiitis is a necrotizing small vessel vasculitis without granulomas. It frequently presents with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage.

vis.alt: Pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis in microscopic polyangiitis
vis.caption: Renal biopsy demonstrates pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in MPA. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Circulating perinuclear ANCA or **p-ANCA** targeting **myeloperoxidase** or MPO-ANCA is detected in **70 to 85 percent** of patients with microscopic polyangiitis. Anti-MPO autoantibodies bind cytokine-primed neutrophils, triggering an uncontrolled oxidative burst, granular enzyme release, and direct cytotoxic lysis of microvascular endothelium.
steps.say: Up to 85 percent of microscopic polyangiitis patients carry anti-myeloperoxidase antibodies. These autoantibodies trigger neutrophil activation and endothelial damage.

nodes.label: Circulating anti-MPO autoantibodies bind primed neutrophils
Neutrophil respiratory burst and granular proteolysis

steps.tx: Renal involvement occurs in over **90 percent** of patients with MPA, manifesting as **pauci-immune necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis**. Light microscopy reveals segmental glomerular fibrinoid necrosis and extensive crescent formation, while immunofluorescence microscopy confirms the absence of significant immune complex or complement deposition.
steps.say: Renal disease affects over 90 percent of MPA patients as necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis. Immunofluorescence confirms a pauci-immune pattern without immune complexes.

rows: Reflects acute rupture of glomerular basement membrane
Distinguishes MPA from lupus nephritis and anti-GBM disease
Rules out subendothelial or mesangial immune complex deposition

steps.tx: Unlike granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis is clearly distinguished by the **complete absence of granulomatous inflammation** in the upper or lower respiratory tracts. Patients with MPA do not develop destructive saddle-nose deformities, cartilaginous destruction, subglottic stenosis, or cavitating parenchymal lung nodules on chest imaging.
steps.say: Microscopic polyangiitis lacks granulomatous airway inflammation. Patients do not develop saddle-nose deformity, subglottic stenosis, or cavitating pulmonary nodules.

left.title: Microscopic polyangiitis
points: No saddle-nose deformity or subglottic stenosis

right.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
points: Cavitary pulmonary nodules and nasal destruction

steps.tx: Fibrosing **interstitial lung disease** occurs in **15 to 30 percent** of MPO-ANCA positive patients with microscopic polyangiitis. Characteristically showing a usual interstitial pneumonia or nonspecific interstitial pneumonia pattern on high-resolution chest CT, ILD frequently precedes systemic vasculitic features and confers significant long-term mortality.
steps.say: Interstitial lung disease complicates up to 30 percent of MPO-ANCA positive cases. Interstitial fibrosis often precedes systemic vasculitis and worsens long-term prognosis.

nodes.label: Chronic MPO-ANCA mediated microvascular alveolar inflammation
Fibroblast activation and progressive collagen deposition
UIP or NSIP pattern on chest CT with restrictive lung defect

steps.tx: First-line remission induction for organ- or life-threatening MPA combines high-dose systemic glucocorticoids with either **rituximab at 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses** or **intravenous cyclophosphamide**. Landmark randomized clinical trials have established equivalent efficacy between rituximab and cyclophosphamide for achieving complete clinical remission.
steps.say: Remission induction for severe MPA combines glucocorticoids with either rituximab or cyclophosphamide. Both agents demonstrate equivalent remission induction rates.

rows: 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 weeks or 1,000 mg twice
Preferred for relapsing disease and fertility preservation
Intravenous pulses 15 mg/kg every 2 to 3 weeks
Preferred in severe pulmonary hemorrhage or renal crisis
IV methylprednisolone pulse followed by rapid oral taper
PEXIVAS-reduced steroid regimen lowers serious infection risk

steps.tx: The landmark **PEXIVAS trial** demonstrated that routine **therapeutic plasma exchange** did not reduce the composite incidence of death or end-stage renal disease in severe AAV presenting with advanced renal failure or alveolar hemorrhage. Consequently, plasma exchange is now reserved specifically for concurrent anti-GBM disease or severe hypoxemic alveolar hemorrhage refractory to therapy.
steps.say: The PEXIVAS trial showed that routine plasma exchange did not prevent death or end-stage kidney failure. Plasma exchange is reserved for refractory alveolar hemorrhage or anti-GBM overlap.

left.title: PEXIVAS trial findings
points: Plasma exchange did not reduce death or ESRD
Reduced-dose steroids showed equal efficacy and fewer infections

right.title: Current plasma exchange indications
points: Severe hypoxemic alveolar hemorrhage failing therapy

steps.tx: Remission maintenance relies on **rituximab at 500 mg every 6 months** or daily oral **azathioprine at 2 mg/kg**, continued for at least **24 months** following complete clinical remission. Concomitant prophylaxis against **Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia** with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is mandatory throughout immunosuppressive therapy to prevent fatal opportunistic pulmonary infections.
steps.say: Remission maintenance requires rituximab every 6 months or azathioprine for at least 24 months. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with co-trimoxazole is mandatory.

vis.alt: Long-term immunosuppression and infection prophylaxis in ANCA vasculitis
vis.caption: Maintenance immunosuppression requires vigilant Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis. Credit: StewardMD.
